svg.title: Red protein suppresses breast-cancer lung metastasis
svg.desc: Model figure assembled from the original shaded artwork. Red protein localizes to the outer mitochondrial membrane, binds DRP1, and blocks DRP1 binding to the green partner, oligomerization, fission, and fission-induced UPRmt. Without UPRmt, mitochondrial proteins do not enter the nucleus to induce EMT, and lung metastasis is suppressed.

g.text: Red protein suppresses breast-cancer lung metastasis

text.tspan: It docks on the outer mitochondrial membrane, holds DRP1 away from the green partner,
and thereby shuts off fission-induced UPRmt, nuclear EMT signaling, and lung colonization.

g.inkscape:label: Story path
g.text: no green-partner binding, no fission, no UPRmt
mitochondrial proteins do not enter the nucleus

text.tspan: The red protein resides in mitochondria and can
relocalize to the outer membrane. The organelle
stays elongated when fission is blocked.
Red protein binds DRP1 and blocks its contact
with the green partner, so DRP1 cannot oligomerize.
DRP1 would assemble on the green
turn on EMT genes. That relay stops.

g.text: LEGEND · drawings are from the original figure

text.tspan: moves to the nucleus if UPRmt is on
Red protein is the brake. Blocking DRP1 stops fission, UPRmt, EMT transcription, and lung metastasis.
